message:
Added new command line options to cp2k_driver

* qmmm_link_type - IMOMM, PSEUDO or QM_KIND. IMOMM and PSEUDO
  do nothing and QM_KIND suppresses QM-MM links	from PSF,
  labels QM and	MM regions as separate molecules,
  changes QM_KIND of inner boundary QM atoms to qmmm_link_qm_kind,
  and adds qmmm_link_n_electrons to DFT_CHARGE for each link.
* qmmm_link_qm_kind  - qm kind used when qmmm_link_type=QM_KIND
* qmmm_same_lattice - if true, use original MM lattice for QM calc
* qmmm_use_mm_charges - if true (default) use MM charges to compute DFT charge
* qmmm_link_fix_pbc - if true (default), fix positions of outer link atoms
  when a QM/MM link crosses a periodic boundary

Other changes required to support these new options:
 * call get_qm_list() before writing PSF file since write_psf() now needs
   the list of QM/MM link bonds so it can remove them from topology

author: James Kermode <james.kermode@gmail.com>
message:
Fix symbol resolution issue by loading _quippy with RTLD_GLOBAL

The issue was that libAtoms.so has an undefined reference to f90wrap_abort_
which must be resolved to the implementation in _quippy.so at load time.
By default, Python loads extension modules with RTLD_LOCAL, which makes
symbols in _quippy.so invisible to other shared libraries like libAtoms.so.

This commit adds sys.setdlopenflags(os.RTLD_NOW | os.RTLD_GLOBAL) before
importing _quippy, making the f90wrap_abort symbol globally visible so that
libAtoms can properly resolve it. The flags are restored after import to
avoid affecting other module loads.

This fixes GAP/SOAP test failures where incorrect energies and forces were
being calculated due to error handling not working correctly.

Fixes #695

message:
Merge Hiten's PR along with my revisions afterwards

This work is over a year old and certain aspects were unfinished.
Things may break. We are merging so we can simply continue from
where we stopped instead of rethinking error handling mechanism
all over again.

Briefly, because BLAST is now run asynchronously we needed a new
mechanism to surface the errors raised during the execution back
to the user. These include things like incorrect advanced params,
BLAST segfaulting, job getting deleted after a while, etc. The
simplest approach is to check the job's exit status and stderr
before generating report.

Conflicts were resolved in the following files during merge:
lib/sequenceserver/blast/formatter.rb
lib/sequenceserver/blast/job.rb
public/js/sequenceserver.js
lib/sequenceserver/job.rb

author: Anurag Priyam <anurag08priyam@gmail.com>
message:
Do not load RubyGems ourselves.

When gem is installed RubyGems creates wrappers that inject RubyGems into the
environment. So requiring rubygem in bin/sequenceserver is not warranted.

During development, it's recommended to use `bundle exec bin/sequenceserver` or
`rackup -I lib` where `bundle exec` and `rackup` will ensure RubyGems is loaded.

IIRC, `mod_passenger` loads RubyGems and activates Gemfile by default.

In short, we don't need to `require 'rubygems'` anywhere in our code base, If a
user's deploy setup is not behaving as expected, options such as setting
environment variables (like RUBYOPT) or a deploy script that loads RubyGems
should be explored first.

Signed-off-by: Anurag Priyam <anurag08priyam@gmail.com>

Tighten dependency.

* Depend on Bundler 1.2.x.
* Instruct Travis to use latest Bundler for installing dependencies.
* Depend on Sinatra 1.3.x.

SequenceServer makes use of the latest release of its dependencies.  This is
primarily because I refer to the source code of the latest release, and might
inadvertently introduce a change that depends on the latest public API.

I think SequenceServer should always depend on the latest, stable release. It
makes things easier for everyone.  You have the latest enhancements: bugfixes,
performance improvements, fixes for security vulnerabilities, newer API that
has more to offer, etc.

author: Anurag Priyam <anurag08priyam@gmail.com>
message:
ui: improve presentation of blast results [#10]

SequenceServer visually separates (into boxes) results of each input query. For
better visual separation, the boxes were alternately colored with a light shade
of pink and green. However, different colors to represent conceptually same
entities is more confusing than helpful (takes time getting used to). Besides,
the pink looked quite ugly. The boxes are all uniform now with a light green
background and a border around the one in focus. To enhance readability, the
actual blast output (hit) is presented against a white background with bigger
fonts. Furthermore, database info and references get their own separate
sections, which are simply chunks of text marked with a light border. While the
entire result is overlaid on a white background instead of (previously used)
dark gray which hurt the eyes.

Signed-off-by: Anurag Priyam <anurag08priyam@gmail.com>

message:
Use -target_only option when fetching sequences from BLAST+ database.

BLAST+ sometimes returns more than one sequences for an accession number when
querying nr/nt database. The sequences returned are identical except their id.
This behaviour is unintuitive and causes SequenceServer to warn users that the
databases might be incorrectly formatted. Using -target_only ensures BLAST+
will return the exact match for the queried accession.

author: Tadas Tamosauskas <tadastamo@gmail.com>
message:
Add Cross-Site-Forgery-Request (CSRF) protection

Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) is a type of malicious exploit of a
website where unauthorized commands are transmitted from a user that
the web application trusts. Without the user's knowledge, the attacker
tricks the victim into performing actions on their behalf.
i.e. copy-pasting JS commands to dev tools console or similar.
This vulnerability exploits the trust that a site has in a user's browser,
allowing attackers to perform actions on behalf of the user without
their consent or awareness.

To protect from this attack we're adding a crsf token, that is generated
randomly, stored in session, and added to each form submission/POST
request. Requests fail if the token value submitted does not match
the value in the session, significantly reducing the risk of malicious
or unintentional requests on behalf of the user.

While this is not really necessary for locally running instances or
public instances, folks hosting their own private instances or exposing
locally hosted instances to the internet will benefit from this.

message:
ui: display advanced parameters in a modal

The user can request to see the allowed advanced parameters by clicking on the
"question mark icon" next to the input box for advanced parameters.

I borrowed the idea from how Github and Gmail display "keyboard shortcuts" when
you press "?".  Showing a list of advanced parameters that can be used with
SequenceServer is a much similar use case.

Also, a "question mark icon" is a widely acknowledged metaphor for "what is
this?" or "help!".

And displaying and hiding advanced parameters no longer interferes with the
index generated for a multi-query BLAST.

author: Anurag Priyam <anurag08priyam@gmail.com>
message:
deploy: fix suburi deployment quirks (fix #49)

Rack [specifies][1] `SCRIPT_NAME` environment variable be set and
available to apps to be able to determine their virtual location.
Sinatra's URL helper, `Sinatra::Base#url`, takes `SCRIPT_NAME` (and
other parameters) into account for URL construction. Lets use it to
guard against broken URLs when deploying SequenceServer to a sub URI.

Note:

* I am not sure how to, or if it even makes sense to use the url helper
  in search.js. As a workaround, the AJAX request is fired to the
  current URL. This works because:

    1. only the main page loads and uses search.js

    2. the same route that renders the main page and handles BLAST
       queries, is responsible for AJAX request too (the same route
       behaves differently for different types of requests).

* The deployment scheme needs to ensure that `SCRIPT_NAME` environment
  variable is set. I didn't have to set it on both of my Phusion
  Passenger based test beds.

[1]: http://rack.rubyforge.org/doc/files/SPEC.html

Signed-off-by: Anurag Priyam <anurag08priyam@gmail.com>

author: Anurag Priyam <anurag08priyam@gmail.com>
message:
Validate num_threads setting.

Previously SequenceServer would assume 1 thread if num_threads wasn't set, or
set incorrectly in the config file. I think we should use a default value only
if one wasn't provided by the user. If the user explicitly sets a configuration
value, and it's incorrect, we should alert the user instead. Additionally, we
warn the user if num_threads is greater than 256.

Explicit validation caught an error in our code where num_threads, if not set
in config file, was assumed to be 0 in Ruby 1.8.7.

Signed-off-by: Anurag Priyam <anurag08priyam@gmail.com>

author: Mark Anthony Gibbins <xiy3x0@gmail.com>
message:
list NCBI multi-part BLAST database only once (close #54)

From http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/staff/tao/URLAPI/blastdb.html:

    Large databases are formatted in multiple one-gigabytes volumes, which are
    named using the database.##.tar.gz convention, with ## representing the
    volume number. All relevant volumes are required to reconstitute the
    database. An alias file is, with .nal or .pal extension, is included in the
    00 volume to tie all volumes together. The database can be called using the
    alias name without the extension. For example, to call nt database, simply
    use "-d nt" in the commandline without the quotes.

Previously, SequenceServer would initialize a `Database` object once per
volume, causing the database to be listed as many times as the number of
volumes it was split into.  So when scanning for databases, SequenceServer now
skips past all but alias file of a NCBI multi-part BLAST database, correctly
initializing the database only once.

[ap: use explicit comments in the source code]
[ap: detailed commit message]

Signed-off-by: Mark Anthony Gibbins <xiy3x0@gmail.com>

message:
Remove Database.seqids.

As per the dicussion in 3d928a09 which higlighted a couple of issues
with that approach like high memory consumption or increased startup
time, we revert those changes.

Instead of maintaining a set of accessions per Database in memory, we invoke
blastdbcmd to detect if a given accession is in a particular database or not.

Additionally, we move `which_blastdb` from `Sequence` to `Report` class so that
this method might be invoked when constructing links per hit, which is what the
original intention was. And we only check `querydb` instead of all databases so
as to provide more relevant result.

The feature and solution is courtesy:
Volodymyr Zavidovych <vo.zavidovych@gmail.com> (close #99).

author: Tadas Tamosauskas <tadastamo@gmail.com>
message:
Refactor collapse preferences to store both open and closed states.

If we want an element to be closed by default, in
the previous implementation we would not have been
able to store that state - if a user opened an
element it would remove it from the collapsed
elements array, but would not keep it open on the
consecutive load, because it would fall back to
the default collapsed state.

This change stores both open and closed states,
and uses a new storage key to store the states
to avoid breaking changes due to old storage.

The collapse preferences are now stored in the
localStorage as a JSON object, with the key being
the name of the element and the value being a boolean
indicating whether the element is collapsed or not.

message:
Bundler is no longer a runtime dependency.

Deployment tools like RVM and Passenger anyway activate Gemfile. It doesn't
have to be done from within the application.

Side effect?

While the executable will work perfectly when SequuenceServer is installed as a
RubyGem, running bin/sequenceserver from the repository can fail:

1. If 'sequenceserver' gem is installed, the executable will load the installed
    gem if RubyGems is loaded instead of loading SequenceServer from the
    repository.
2. If 'sequenceserver' gem isn't installed or RubyGems isn't loaded, the
    executable will fail with a stack trace.

To avoid either just `bundle exec bin/sequenceserver` during development or
when trying to use SequenceServer from git.

Signed-off-by: Anurag Priyam <anurag08priyam@gmail.com>

author: Tadas Tamosauskas <tadastamo@gmail.com>
message:
Refactor BLAST::Report to lazily generate reports

In some cases (e.g. when used by some extensions) it is beneficial
to not generate the report files upfront, and only do it when it's
required. Performance gains are significant with large result sets
(i.e. hundreds of MB or GBs) as the data does not need to be
loaded into the process memory.

Lazy method evaluation with memoization allows to achieve just that
without cognitive overload to developer - operations are now only
executed when the methods are invoked, not up-front by default.

Implementation logic was not changed and regression test prepared
upfront is not failing and producing identical results.

author: Vivek Rai <vivekraiiitkgp@gmail.com>
message:
BLAST to XML.

Previously SequenceServer BLASTed query sequences to HTML format. Subsequently
the HTML was parsed, using regular expressions, to get hit id and coordinates,
prettified and presented to the user. It was a nightmare to maintain and extend.

We now BLAST to XML, parse the XML using Ox -- a self contained, Ruby 1.8.7
compatible, fast XML parser -- to create an object representation of BLAST
results. Subsequently we render an ERb template to generate HTML report.

We are thus able to take fine-grained control over HTML report generated. To
begin with, we generate NCBI like HTML report. Later, we will make data from
BLAST result available in browser via data- attributes or JSON, thus paving way
for generating graphical overview and filtering of results based on e-value etc.

And the code feels manageable and extendable now.

[ap: commit message]

author: Vivek Rai <vivekraiiitkgp@gmail.com>
message:
Build index of seq_ids for each database

Each Database object now contains a set of seq_ids contained within it.
This allows us to determine whether a Database contains a particular
sequence id or not.

e.g., database.include?(accession) => true/false

Another use of this feature is that it provides reverse lookup i.e.,
find which database contains this particular sequence. However, in many
cases a single sequence id can be present in multiple databases at a
time. We return all of the values and not just the first value.

author: Anurag Priyam <anurag08priyam@gmail.com>
message:
fetch BLAST results via AJAX on the onsubmit event and not onclick

`onsubmit` is triggered whenever the form is about to be submitted, regardless
of the input mode.  `onclick`, on the other hand, won't be triggered if the
form submission was triggered by pressing `Enter` key.

The rationale for this change is not only pragmatic, but also a bug that caused
the placeholder text for advanced parameters to be submitted on some old
browsers that don't support placeholders natively.  On such browsers,
SequenceServer mocks a placeholder by setting `value` attribute of the input
(text) box to the desired text, and removing it just before submitting the form
(if not already removed when filling the form).  However, fetching BLAST
results on `onclick` caused the form to be submitted before SequenceServer
could remove the mock placeholder text.

Thanks to Jonna Katharina Kulmuni, and Fourmidable for helping discover and
squash this issue.

Signed-off-by: Anurag Priyam <anurag08priyam@gmail.com>

React router is used to work with search and reports page together as a
single-page app, while SystemJS is used to provide a module framework -
ES6 module is used within our code while SystemJS takes care of loading

the process. Most importantly, jquery 2.1.4 from 1.11.2. Furthermore,
HTML5 Shiv was removed. This shouldn't be an issues as SequenceServer
doesn't support IE8 and below. For simplicity, assets are minified in
one bundle (one each for JS & CSS).

Since CodeClimate can now be run locally (via docker) and supports
RuboCop, ES Lint and CSS Lint; we move to it for static analysis.

author: Anurag Priyam <anurag08priyam@gmail.com>
message:
Mega refactor - with focus on improving the CLI and setup.

Changes
-------
We now have an equivalent CLI switch for every option one could set via
configuration file. If the same option is set in configuration file and
passed from command line, command line will take precedence.

Database dir is now a compulsory option and it's the only compulsory option.

Host is now configurable.

format-databases subcommand has been removed in favour of -m switch.
And -l & -u will respectively list BLAST+ databases and FASTA files
yet to be converted into a BLAST+ database.

Can update configuration file from command line using -s switch.

Can run SequenceServer in interactive mode (-i).

When using SequenceServer for the first time:
  - If BLAST+ not installed, offer to install.
  - If no BLAST+ database in database dir, offer to create BLAST+ databases.

Simple plug-in architecture:
  - Optionally load a Ruby script after initialisation.

Refactoring
-----------
SequenceServer module defines all functionality needed to setup, start and run.
  - Removed DatabaseFormatter module. Made the functions a part of SequenceServer
    module.
  - Blast module is now mixed into SequenceServer instead of SequenceServer::App.
  - SequenceServer::App is now just a controller. Rack entry point is
    `SequenceServer.call`

Squashed sequencehelpers.rb and sequence.rb into one - sequence.rb.

Rename sinatralikelogformatter.rb to logger.rb and have it define a custom
logger with the same logging format.

Switched to Slop in bin/sequenceserver.

SequenceServer#verbose? -> true if development mode.

Symbolize keys from config.yml.

message:
blast.rb: reliably capture stdout, stderr, and exit status of a process

The changes made in the last commit didn't work for blastn when called with
task option except when the task was 'megablast'.  And I have no friggin idea
why.  A simple workaround is to employ bash's I/O redirection: redirect stdout

author: Anurag Priyam <anurag08priyam@gmail.com>
message:
ui logic rewrite (closes #8)

We now poll for user input change rather than trying to bind to all
possible events - keydown, cut, paste and what not. Polling captures it
all, so we define our UI behavior only once. This makes our code less
prone to errors, and much more manageable.

Another significant change is that we no longer reset the entire form in
one go. Instead, we only change the form just enough to reflect a change
in the user input. Advantage here is that if a user has already selected
a blast method, or databases to blast against, before he/she pastes the
input sequence, we don't reset the existing selection unless it is
incompatible with the input sequence type.

This is a major overhaul to our UI 'intelligence', made better over
various iterations, albeit a little heavy on the browser. This should
take good care of #8.

author: Anurag Priyam <anurag08priyam@gmail.com>
message:

on each invocation of `settings.log`.  This is sub-optimal and looses all
customization made to the Logger instance -- log level and log format, during
startup.  Removing the surrounding `Proc.new` ensures the same instance is

Upgrade to Bootstrap 3, and a more modern, vanilla Bootstrap 3 UI.

Development of new features will gain from Bootstrap 3 upgrade. And the new UI
aligns better with SequenceServer's minimal, intuitive, and elegant philosophy.

No changes were made to the user work flow.

SequenceServer will no longer pop-up users to tweet us though. Instead, I
placed the Twitter button in the footer. And citation, which was previously
randomised together with marketing quotes, is also always visible in footer
now.

NOTES:
* Excluded Carousel and Glyphicons from Bootstrap build. Using FontAwesome 4
  instead of Glyphicons.
* Removed dependency on unmaintained jquery.activity.js. Using FontAwesome's
  spinner instead.
* Re-formatted search.erb.
* Include all JS just before closing 'body' tag, which improves page load time.
* Merged databases.erb into search.erb - easier to maintain.

author: Anurag Priyam <anurag08priyam@gmail.com>
message:
Depend on Bundler 1.2.x.

Not specifying a version number will cause RubyGems to settle for _any_ release
of Bundler that it might find on the user's system.  But the locally installed,
older release of Bundler might not be API compatible with newer release that
SequenceServer actually depends on, and might cause SequenceServer to break on
the user's machine.

We need at least Bundler 1.0.13.  But since I refer to the code of latest
release, it is probably best to depend on same, lest I should introduce a
change that depends on the public API provided by the newest release.

We depend on Bundler 1.2.x assuming it follows Semantic Versioning [1], so the
public API won't change in a point release.

[1]: http://semver.org/

Signed-off-by: Anurag Priyam <anurag08priyam@gmail.com>

message:
Clear SequenceServer::Database.collection after each test context

Test suites may initialise SequenceServer using different databases
directories in spec/. Many of the databases in the different subdirs are
essentially the same (same content, same display name), just formatted a
little different: v4, v5, with or without -parse_seqids option. This can
result in an accumulation of databases with the same name in the process
and cause confusion. For example, Capybara test that require selecting a
database in the interface based on name may fail because of ambiguous
matches.

Automatically clearing SequenceServer::Database.collection fixes this
problem.

Update BLAST::Report API. Fix NCBI link generator.

An HSP now holds a pointer to the Hit object it belongs to. Hit to Query. And
Query to Report. Leveraging this, we define Hit#querydb which simply forwards
to Report#querydb, move Report#which_blastdb to Hit#whichdb, and extend Hit
class with Links module instead of Report. This approach feels "just right".

Update link generators accordingly, fix NCBI link generator while at it (which
was broken because we had begun using Hit#accession instead of Hit#id several
commits back and thus couldn't infer if the hit was from nr database), and
simplify Report a bit.

author: nuin <nuin@genedrift.org>
message:
Add methods for gene link generation in SequenceServer module

Three methods - 'jbrowse', 'mod_gene_link' and 'agr_gene_link' - have been added to the SequenceServer module. These methods generate sequence retrieval links. The 'jbrowse' method generates links for sequence data in JBrowse and JBrowse2. The 'mod_gene_link' and 'agr_gene_link' methods generate links for gene data for the Model Organism Database (MOD) and the Alliance of Genome Resources (AGR) respectively.

author: Anurag Priyam <anurag08priyam@gmail.com>
message:
Distinguish between small and large reports

If total number of hits for all query sequences is greater than 500,
we call it a 'veryBig' report. 500 hit sequences allows displaying
500 hits for a single query (503 visualisations), or one hit each
for 500 queries (1501 visualisations on the page).

Small reports have alignments overview shown by default. Large reports
have all visualisations hidden by default.

Other bug fixes and refactoring:
- Set 'in' class on SVG containers during initialisation if collapsed
  prop was set to false
- Set 'collapse' class in Grapher component instead of in each Graph

The change had an unintended consequence of disabling the help
modal for advanced features.

I'd argue that https://github.com/wurmlab/sequenceserver/issues/695
is a bit misleading - it is expected for HTML
labels to be clickable. Clicking on an input field label should
focus the input field, which it was doing. I don't think this should
change.

It just happens that the help modal trigger is crammed into the label
too, so it can perhaps get confusing when the two elements next to each other are clickable and react to the same hover - perhaps the latter needs
to change instead?

message:
sequenceserver: set `$PROGRAM_NAME` after parsing command line arguments

`$0` captures how the executable was invoked:

user passes an invalid option or subcommand. However, setting `$PROGRAM_NAME`
sets `$0` to the same value. So we set it after command line options have been
parsed and immediately before launching SequenceServer.

author: Anurag Priyam <anurag08priyam@gmail.com>
message:
guess sequence type on the client side

This should offer visible performance improvements in most SequenceServer
setup.  First, this avoids the repeated network overhead in determining
sequence type.  Second, JS is faster than Ruby.  Third, the implementation
should be more performant than its server side counterpart.

Client computers are reasonably well powered nowadays.  It is well justified to
offload as much processing as possible to the client side :).

`post '/' do ... end` code block is also simplified as a result, since there is
only one AJAX request (for BLASTing) that it has to handle now.

Signed-off-by: Anurag Priyam <anurag08priyam@gmail.com>

message:
Split off sourcemaps from the minified JS

Configure webpack to compile a separate sourcemaps file instead of
using the default eval inline source maps.

This removes a combined ~3MB from the two JS bundles (the separate
source map files are not loaded by default onto the user's browsers).

Not using eval mode source maps is a bit slower, but also makes it
easier to configure CSP (for the cloud version) with strong defaults

author: Anurag Priyam <anurag08priyam@gmail.com>
message:
exercise caution when coupling blastn with advanced parameters (close #80)

Commit 'blast: execute `blastn`, not `megablast`, when `blastn` is selected'
caused BLAST to fail if one used advanced parameters in conjunction with
`blastn`.  This would happen because of malformed shell command: missing
whitespace between two consecutive options, or more than one `-task ...`
options.  SequenceServer alleviates the issue by being a little careful when
adding advanced parameters by itself.

Signed-off-by: Anurag Priyam <anurag08priyam@gmail.com>

author: Anurag Priyam <anurag08priyam@gmail.com>
message:
Optimise rendering process

First update transfers responseJSON to Report.state so that summary
overview and circos can be rendered. Subsequent updates add Query, Hit,
and HSP components to Report.state.results which are then inserted into
the page by React. The first cycle is started with the call to setState
in setStateFromJSON and subsequent cycles are is queued in
componentDidUpdate. componentDidUpdate is run after the DOM has been
updated (that is, virtual DOM has been applied). The use of setTimeout
ensures that the browser gets a break from the rendering process and can
respond to user interactions. Because we queue the next update after DOM
has been updated, the setTimeout interval does not need to be very high.
Finally, the number of each HSPs rendered in a cycle should be small.
This is because the browser is blocked from responding to user
interactions such as click till it has finished the current cycle.
However, if this number is too small, like 1, the time required to
render the whole report increases. The implemented threshold of 3 is 3
times faster than rendering only 1 HSP in each update cycle.

The rendering process is further optimised by implementing the
shouldComponentUpdate life-cycle method for Query, Hit, and HSP
components. This avoids re-rendering (including to virtual-dom).
This causes the view sequence button per-hit to break as it
relies on Hit.state to activate SequenceViewer.

API wise, hits are no longer nested inside queries, and hsps are no
longer nested inside hits. This has created minor breaking changes
that should be addressed next.

author: Anurag Priyam <anurag08priyam@gmail.com>
message:
Finalise how errors are communicated back to browser

- Error classes should define http_status which is used by Sinatra to
  set the appropriate response status. If none is provided, status is
  set to 500.
- Error classes should have a message (used in modal body), and may
  optionally provide a title (used in modal header), and additional
  info for debugging (displayed using a pre tag). Error class is
  used as title if one isn't explicitly set. Additional info may be
  backtrace or info parsed from output of a program.
- Accordingly we define three error classes:
  - SystemError (500). BLAST crashed before generating output, disk
    full, corrupt or incompatible BLASTDB files. Recovering from
    SystemError will inevitably requires Unix skills
  - InputError (400). Problem with query, selected databases, or
    advanced parameters. Recoverable by rerunning BLAST.
  - NotFound (404). Job has been deleted.

Signed-off-by: Anurag Priyam <anurag08priyam@gmail.com>

message:
Remove SequenceServer::App.binaries.

Now we just export NCBI BLAST+ binaries directory to PATH. It will work since
all command are executed from SequenceServer in a sub-shell.

How do we then ensure that NCBI BLAST+ is installed? When SequenceServer is
launched, it must run blastdbcmd to look for BLAST databases. If blastdbcmd
exists we assume other BLAST binaries to be present and conclude NCBI BLAST+ is
installed on the user's system. But if blastdbcmd can't be found, we tell the
user to install NCBI BLAST+ like before.

All in all, this simplifies the code to a good extent.

author: Anurag Priyam <anurag08priyam@gmail.com>
message:
Reset location.hash when user submits a BLAST request (close #34).

Once the BLAST results are available users shouldn't have to scroll down
themselves to see the result.  SS does this by setting location.hash to
'result' once the BLAST results have been fetched causing browser to jump
to the BLAST results.

Now, if users need to re-blast, they will have to go back to the search form,
edit parameters, and click BLAST.  There are three ways a user can go back to
the search form: scroll up, refresh page, hit back button.  `location.hash` is
retained in the first two approach.  And browsers don't react if one tries to
set `location.hash` to the same value that it holds.  So SS wouldn't jump to
results for the second time if the user scrolled up, or did a page refresh to
get back to the search form, after viewing the results.  Instead SS would stay
at the current scroll location.

As a workaround, SS now resets `location.hash` to '' when user clicks BLAST.
And sets it back to 'result', as usual, when BLAST results are available.
Effectively, SS should always _jump_ to results after a successful BLAST.

Signed-off-by: Anurag Priyam <anurag08priyam@gmail.com>

Passenger redirects `STDERR` to Apache's error logs.  However, SequenceServer
logged to `STDOUT` making it difficult for admins to tap into Passenger's
logging mechanism for SequenceServer deployment.  Fixed it now.

On a related note, Passenger's log level can be tweaked with the
`PassengerLogLevel` option in the relevant Apache virtual host entry.  See [1].

Note: Though I haven't tested it on other deployment environment, the fix
should _ideally_ apply to all of them.

[1]: http://modrails.com/documentation/Users%20guide%20Apache.html#_passengerloglevel_lt_integer_gt

author: Anurag Priyam <anurag08priyam@gmail.com>
message:
Remove to_fasta.

to_fasta was meant to add a def line to query sequence, if missing; and
uniquify query sequence ids by appending a number to duplicates.

Older versions of BLAST+ used to crash if query didn't have def line. BLAST+
2.2.25 (SequenceServer's minimum requirement) and higher handle missing def
line in query sequence gracefully. Thus adding def line to the query isn't
needed anymore.

Uniquification of query sequence ids came as a fix for #109. However, recent
changes (SHA: d377d3bc in particular ) obsoletes the fix. BLAST+ internally
numbers the query sequences 1, 2, 3, ..., n. Numbering done by BLAST+ is
available in XML output, on which our HTML result is now based. We use the
numbering done by BLAST+ to created unique HTML ids and thus index doesn't fail
anymore.

Signed-off-by: Anurag Priyam <anurag08priyam@gmail.com>

author: Anurag Priyam <anurag08priyam@gmail.com>
message:
Fix evalue bug.

evalues that weren't outputted by BLAST in scientific notation were rounded to
two decimal places, causing 0.001 to be shown as 0.00. Now we render in pretty
scientific notation all evalues less than 1 and greater than or equal to 10.

Rendering all evalues less than 1 in scientific notation avoids the above bug.
It's easier to compare 1.2e-1 to 2.6e-5 than 0.12 to 2.6e-5. Similarly, 1-100
is easier to compare in non-scientific notation. But because we are doing e-1,
for consistency it's probably a good idea to start with e+1 (10) on this side.
Hopefully we will never have to render evalues greater than or equal to 10.

Signed-off-by: Anurag Priyam <anurag08priyam@gmail.com>

author: Anurag Priyam <anurag08priyam@gmail.com>
message:
dynamically derive configuration options

In 870aae27 I had defined parse_config which would set the value of each
configuration option. While this allowed for an explicit configuration
management throughout the app, the method parse_config in intself was
essentially inelegant, as it had to know in advance how to handle each
option.

The beauty of Sinatra::Base.set, and the elegance of Ruby's proc (yup,
the closure properties) makes it possible to derive configuration
options dynamically by defining by defining a proc for each setting
which knows exactly how to process its value.

builtin Array#sort method to sort a list of dbs. Then call sort! on the
list of scanned databases in the scan_blast_db method, so that dbs are

as we rely on the db index value returned from the form to pick up the
right db for blasting.

message:
ui: remove the close button from the top of modal windows

Only one way of doing things should be less confusing to the users.  One may
argue that with two buttons a user can click on whichever is closer to the
pointer.  But in my experience users unconsciously reach out for the same
button all the time.  I do.  We keep the lower one, that says 'close' or 'got
it', because the user is expected to read the text -- we have small meaningful
messages anyway -- before she dismisses the modal dialog saying, "Fine. Thank
you."

Thanks to Yannick for the tip :).

Add a basic cloud sharing client

Cloud sharing is a new SequenceServer feature that allows sharing
search results pages with anyone. Since SequenceServer is a gem
that a lot of people run locally on their machines, sharing results
from it may be difficult. This feature allows uploading job results
to an instance hosted by SequenceServer Cloud and getting back
a shareable URL accessible from the public internet to those
who have a copy of the URL.

message:
Inform users about network and server timeout errors.

Timeout or network errors previously appeared to the user as "a flicker of
spinner followed by no results or an empty modal", leaving them to figure
out for themselves what exactly happened. Not good.

Detecting timeout errors is tricky. We can be sure that the response will be
empty if server timed-out. But empty response can be caused due to myriad of
network issues.

So we check for empty response and notify users that either the server timed
out (and hence she should contact admin), or there's a temporary network issue
(and hence she should try again later). As a laster resort, the user should
seek help on the forum.

author: Tadas Tamosauskas <tadastamo@gmail.com>
message:
[Performance] Do not perform unnecessary operations in makeblastdb

SequenceServer MAKEBLASTDB wrapper was working in two-steps:
1) invoke #scan - this was eagerly scanning for formatted,
  unformatted and DBs that may require reformatting and storing
  them in instance variables
2) whenever any makeblast operation was performed, it relied on scan
  being run beforehand to populate the instance variables and was
  using these values to perform listing, formatting and reformatting
  operations.

When SequienceServer.init was invoked (any time the web server starts
or the CLI binary is launched) it was calling makeblastdb.scan regardless
of whether it will format/reformat the databases. This was rather slow
on large database dirs (I saw upwards of a minute on a large dir).

This change refactors MAKEBLASTDB wrapper to only scan for DBs to format
or reformat when it is actually going to perform any of these operations.

Now the class does not rely on running #scan beforehand to perform any
operations, and invokes the data gathering methods lazilly (i.e. only
when gathering data is required), making sure it does not perform
any slow operations when they are not necessary.

author: Anurag Priyam <anurag08priyam@gmail.com>
message:
ui: do not guess sequence type for queries less than 10 characters (#72)

This was the original behavior.  But to make BLAST method autoselection easier,
I had changed this behavior a few commits back so that SS would _literally_
assume ultrashort queries to be protein.  But now that SS notifies user of the
sequence type detected, it needs to be a little more vigilant.  Telling a user
that 'aa' is a protein sequence is kind of embarrassing.  Hence reverting SS
back to the old behavior -- do not guess sequence type if the length of the
query is less than 10 characters.  So how does SS autoselect BLAST method when
the sequence type is unknown.  Short sequences are _most likely_ protein.
Based on this assumption, and the database type selected SS pre-selects the
BLAST method it thinks is the most appropriate.  And presents a list of
alternatives in a drop down menu next to the BLAST button.

author: Anurag Priyam <anurag08priyam@gmail.com>
message:
ui: make alternate blast method selection from dropdown 'usable' (#72)

When SS can't uniquely determine a BLAST method to use for the given input, it
sets the blast button to the one it thinks is most likely, and presents
possible options in a dropdown list, generated dynamically as the user input
changes, next to the BLAST button.  Now if the dropdown list was generated more
than once before a page refresh, selecting an alternate BLAST method from the
dropdown list might or might not have worked.  And whether it worked or not,
the BLAST button would jiggle more than once.  The cause?  I was attaching to
the click event a function to swap BLAST methods _every time_ the list was
generated.  So when the user clicked on an alternate BLAST method from the
dropdown list, the same event handler was executed multiple times, sometimes
un-swapping BLAST methods and jiggling the BLAST button each time.  Solution?
Don't bind to dynamically created elements; use event bubbling.

Signed-off-by: Anurag Priyam <anurag08priyam@gmail.com>

author: Tadas Tamosauskas <tadastamo@gmail.com>
message:
Refactor collapse preferences to store both open and closed states.

If we want an element to be closed by default, in
the previous implementation we would not have been
able to store that state - if a user opened an
element it would remove it from the collapsed
elements array, but would not keep it open on the
consecutive load, because it would fall back to
the default collapsed state.

This change stores both open and closed states,
and uses a new storage key to store the states
to avoid breaking changes due to old storage.

The collapse preferences are now stored in the
localStorage as a JSON object, with the key being
the name of the element and the value being a boolean
indicating whether the element is collapsed or not.

author: ivopieniak <ivo.pieniak@gmail.com>
message:
Report Optimisation

We are looping over the queries to determine the number of hits
1) If the number of hits exceeds 500, we subtract the number of queries
   by 1, thus reducing the amount of queries spliced in each cycle.
   Therefore, the query that exceeds 500 is passed to the next render
   cycle
2) If the hit number = 500 one or multiple queries are passed for
   rendering
3) If the query number = number of all the queries in the JSON file and
   the num of hits is lower than 500 then this condition is satisfied.

Signed-off-by: ivopieniak <ivo.pieniak@gmail.com>

The current docker file simply installed the latest sequenceserver gem
to the container. This didn't work for beta releases which require --pre
switch to be used. Further, the setup required gems to be published to
RubyGems before pushing the corresponding tag to GitHub (otherwise the
automated build will end up creating a docker image with new tag but
with old version of SequenceServer. Clearly, this is not ideal. The best
way to remain in sync is to build docker image from the fresh git clone
provided by automated build. To this end, adapt Michał T. Lorenc's
dockerfile from #366 to use COPY instead of downloading tarball from
GitHub.

Signed-off-by: Anurag Priyam <anurag08priyam@gmail.com>

author: Tadas Tamosauskas <tadastamo@gmail.com>
message:
Handle JSON errors as 422

When an issue with a user query or configuration occurs, we were
just raising an exception and the sinatra's error block was
returning 500 error page. When we know the shape of the error
and build a JSON response for it, it's more likely to be a 4**
type of error, so default to 422 for a status in such cases.

This is not ideal, but an improvement when it comes to HTTP status
semantics and also helps manage errors when Sequenceserver is deployed
to a server i.e. passenger can be configured to intercept 500 pages
yet 4** ones would still be handled by the app and display useful
error messages to the user.

author: Anurag Priyam <anurag08priyam@gmail.com>
message:
deploy: fix suburi deployment quirks (fix #49)

Rack [specifies][1] `SCRIPT_NAME` environment variable be set and
available to apps to be able to determine their virtual location.
Sinatra's URL helper, `Sinatra::Base#url`, takes `SCRIPT_NAME` (and
other parameters) into account for URL construction. Lets use it to
guard against broken URLs when deploying SequenceServer to a sub URI.

Note:

* I am not sure how to, or if it even makes sense to use the url helper
  in search.js. As a workaround, the AJAX request is fired to the
  current URL. This works because:

    1. only the main page loads and uses search.js

    2. the same route that renders the main page and handles BLAST
       queries, is responsible for AJAX request too (the same route
       behaves differently for different types of requests).

* The deployment scheme needs to ensure that `SCRIPT_NAME` environment
  variable is set. I didn't have to set it on both of my Phusion
  Passenger based test beds.

[1]: http://rack.rubyforge.org/doc/files/SPEC.html

Signed-off-by: Anurag Priyam <anurag08priyam@gmail.com>

author: Tadas Tamosauskas <tadastamo@gmail.com>
message:
[Performance] Add --optimistic flag that skips DB checks

By default, when running SequenceServer.init i.e. when starting
the web server or runninc CLI commands, it will scan the entire
database_dir entries to find databases that use older (v4) version
or have been created without parse_seqids. If this is the case
it will log a warning.

If all databases are formatted correctly and the user knows it,
running SequenceServer with --optimistic can have a significant
impact on reducing startup times. With vast databse directories
this can be in tens of seconds.

This is because parse_seqids in particular does a lot of IO calls
to scan database directories to determine if seqids metadata files
are missing for each database.

message:
Try to make running Capybara tests on Travis more robust

Sometimes Capybara tests that download a file fail because they find
another file in place of the downloaded file. I think this happens
because clear_downloads method silently fails sometimes. As a result
we end up with multiple files in downloads directory and the tests
pick up the wrong file based on default glob order.

This commit includes makes two changes. First, a warning message is
printed if multiple files are found in the downloads directory when
a single file is expected. Second, the globbed files are sorted by
mtime so that hopefully the most recently downloaded file is picked.

author: Iwo Pieniak <ivo.pieniak@gmail.com>
message:
Ability to import BLAST XML

XML files can now be imported using the new `--import` flag. This
creates a fake job (fake because the job won't be run) and prints the
job id. The XML file is copied to the job directory so that if the user
accidentally deletes the original file, we don't have to worry about it.
Furthermore, we can provide a consistent experience with regards to the
job's lifetime.

API wise, the imported XML file is accessed for report generation using
by calling `BLAST::Job#imported_xml_file`. Also, a boolean property
(`imported_xml`) is set at top-level of the JSON sent to the server
which is used to toggle UI elements.

Caveat: Currently the user must manually visit localhost:4567/job_id to
view the report.

message:
Finished implementation of HexRef

 - Added missing functionality for computing and storing  basis function
   evaluations to HexRef
 - Fixed a few minor bugs in Bernstein implementation
 - Added example demonstrating initialization of HexRef and printing out
   data stored in HexRef

In this first implementation, HexRef uses run-time polymorphism to
switch between Lagrange, Legendre, and Bernstein tensor product basis
evaluations.
Dr. Collins suggested that the desired functionality might be better
implemented by templating over the basis function type and using
compile-time polymorphism.

author: stevenj <stevenj@fftw.org>
message:
updated "known result" for polariton_energy for new fields::integrate-based energy
The new field_energy function, using fields::integrate, gives slightly
different energy results from the old code.  This is because of
different integration weights for the boundary edges...I think the new
version is more reasonable, actually.

Basically, the old code just summed up the energy for every point in
the cell, with uniform integration weight.  The new code is almost the
same, except that at the boundaries, it integrates the boundary pixels
assuming linear interpolation to the points just beyond (or at) the
boundary.  (Points beyond the boundary are assumed zero for
non-periodic boundary conditions.)  I think this should be more
accurate.

Of course, the new result and the old result converge to one another
as the resolution is increased.

which is loses the value of dV0 and may double-count interpolation weights,

and sets the weight to 1 when updating the DFT if include_dV_and_interp=false.

author: stevenj <stevenj@alum.mit.edu>
message:
only allocate separate B and H fields if necessary + many related changed

now, unnecessary H fields are set == B at the pointer level; H is
allocated lazily, just before needed, in PML regions or when mu!=1,
to guarantee consistency

allow invmu to be NULL
allow user-specification of mu != 1 (although no averaging is done yet)

don't use PML equations if unnecessary - in the PML regions, some
components may still be updated with the ordinary equations

fix potential bug in update_EDHB where the PML equations might not have
been used if g1 and g2 were swapped, since that also swaps sigsize_dsig1

the PML equations in nonlinear materials now use the fields, not the
fields multiplied by (1+sigma) etc., to determine the nonlinear
coefficient, which seems more correct (and allows us to switch to the
non-PML equations in more cases)

author: Luochenghuang <Luocheng@uw.edu>
message:
Cache maxwell_data across get_eigenmode_coefficients calls

When computing diffraction efficiencies, get_eigenmode_coefficients is called separately for each (order, polarization) pair. Each call recreates MPB's maxwell_data and recomputes the epsilon grid, which dominates runtime for structures with many geometry objects.

Add an eigenmode_cache field to dft_flux that persists the maxwell_data across calls to get_eigenmode_coefficients on the same monitor. The first call creates the cache; subsequent calls reuse it. The cache is automatically invalidated when the flux monitor is removed or destroyed.

Also add a skip_phase_fix parameter to get_eigenmode. When called with a DiffractedPlanewave, phase fixing is skipped since |alpha|^2 is phase-invariant (the mode-mode self-overlap normfac cancels any global phase factor).

No Python API changes — the caching is transparent. Partially addresses #1533.

author: stevenj <stevenj@fftw.org>
message:
optimizations after profiling
After running the code with profiling (compile with -pg) and analyzing
the results with gprof, I noticed that a lot of time was being wasted
calling volume::io() and volume::iloc() during "startup".  (This
corroborated an earlier observation that the pre-time-stepping code
was taking a long time, several seconds in 3d.)  I've sped up this
greatly by several improvements, summarized as follows:

1) Eliminate loops of the form:
	for (i = 0; i < v.ntot(); ++i) {
		ivec here = v.iloc(c, i);
		...
	}
replacing them with LOOP_OVER_VOL

2) Add special loops LOOP_OVER_VOL_OWNED and LOOP_OVER_VOL_NOTOWNED to
loop just over the owned and not-owned (boundary) points,
respectively.

3) io() was still taking too long, so I replaced it with a io member
   that is recomputed on the rare occasions when the origin is changed.
   To make sure that it gets recomputed, volume::origin is now private,
   and there are functions for getting/setting it.

Plus a few other tricks/optimizations in heavily-called "startup" functions.

author: Luochenghuang <Luocheng@uw.edu>
message:
Handle dispersive materials in eigenmode cache

The eigenmode cache (`maxwell_data` reuse across `get_eigenmode_coefficients` calls) assumed frequency-independent epsilon. For dispersive materials, the cached epsilon grid becomes stale when the eigenmode frequency changes. Detect dispersive media during epsilon grid construction by comparing `get_chi1inv(freq)` vs `get_chi1inv(freq=0)`. When the cache is reused at a different frequency on a dispersive monitor, re-populate the epsilon grid on the existing `maxwell_data` (avoiding full reallocation). New fields on `dft_flux`: `eigenmode_cache_dispersive`, `eigenmode_cache_frequency`. New parameters on `get_eigenmode`/`get_eigenmode_coefficients`: `cache_dispersive`, `cache_frequency` (optional, default NULL for backward compatibility).

author: stevenj <stevenj@fftw.org>
message:
vec(r,z) -> veccyl(r,z); vec2d(x,y) -> vec(x,y)
as a historical artifact, the code used vec(_, _) to indicate cylindrical
coordinates, while vec(_) was 1d and vec(_,_,_) was 3d.  2d was handled by
vec2d(_, _).  It makes much more sense to make cylindrical coordinates the
exception, and so I have implemented this change.

To insure that this does not introduce any bugs into Meep, I implemented
the change in 2 stages.  First, implement veccyl and remove vec(_, _)
constructor -- the compiler catches any uses of the 2 argument vec(_,_)
and I can replace them with veccyl.  Second, remove vec2d and make
vec(_,_) produce a 2d vector.

USER CODE WILL NEED TO BE UPDATED, HOWEVER!  Hopefully, the elimination
of vec2d will clue people in that something has changed.

message:
Add is_frequency_dependent output parameter to get_chi1inv

Add an optional bool *is_frequency_dependent parameter (default NULL) to all get_chi1inv and get_chi1inv_at_pt overloads across structure_chunk, fields_chunk, fields, and structure. When non-NULL, it is set to true if any susceptibility with non-zero sigma or non-zero conductivity is encountered, allowing callers to detect dispersive materials without extra get_chi1inv calls at frequency=0.

author: Luocheng Huang <luochenghuang@gmail.com>
message:
OpenMP parallelize grid initialization (set_epsilon)

The grid initialization loop in set_chi1inv iterates over all grid
points to compute the inverse permittivity tensor. At high resolutions
(e.g., 178M points at resolution 200), this takes minutes on a single
core.

Parallelize the loop with OpenMP (PLOOP_OVER_IVECS_C) when the
material function is thread-safe (standard C++ geometry objects, not
Python callbacks). The trivial[] flags use OpenMP reduction.

A new virtual method material_function::is_thread_safe() returns false
by default (safe for Python callbacks). The geom_epsilon subclass
overrides it to return true unless MATERIAL_USER materials are present.

Measured speedup: 30.7s -> 3.2s at resolution 100 (9.7x with 22 cores).
Set OMP_NUM_THREADS to control parallelism.

message: in fields::solve_cw, use the BiCGSTAB(L) algorithm instead of BiCGSTAB.  With L >= 2, this avoids a known convergence failure in BiCGSTAB for operators (like ours) where the eigenvalues are nearly purely imaginary.  Now, solve_cw converges to arbitrary tolerance (limited by numerical precision, of course) even in > 1d!  Hooray, it works!

author: stevenj <stevenj@alum.mit.edu>
message:
initial merge of mu and epsilon support

Merge of update_e_from_d and update_h_from_b, and unified support for
electric and magnetic susceptibilities.  make check passes, but the
libctl front-end has not been updated yet.   Magnetic materials now
support anisotropic averaging, material dispersion, and
nonlinearity.

Instead of invmu and inveps arrays, we now have a single chi1inv array
that stores 1/(1+chi1) for the first-order susceptibilities chi1.  The
material_function::meaneps function has been replaced by a function
material_function::eff_chi1inv_row that is used for both mu and epsilon
and returns a row of the effective-medium 1/(1+chi1) tensor.  This has
the important consequence that user-specified anisotropic materials are
now possible.  Also, user-controlled effective-medium averaging is
possible, and in particular we can do the proper Kottke averaging for
anisotropic media.

Also, some (diagonal) anisotropy is now supported in the chi2 and chi3
nonlinearities.

author: Ben Bartlett <benjamincbartlett@gmail.com>
message:
Implementation of chunk balancer feature

CONTEXT: This feature uses empirical data about the timings of each MPI process to adjust the chunk sizes to achieve optimal load balancing for repeated simulations, such as iterations in an optimization run. Processes which are consistently slow and overworked will have their chunk sizes reduced for the next iteration of an optimization run, and underworked processes will handle larger chunks. This approach has the advantage that it implicitly incorporates variable load between different machines running the MPI processes.

SCOPE:
- Added abstract class for chunk balancer
- Added DefaultChunkBalancer implementation, which adjusts chunk sizes according to per-process working time (ignoring all-all comms) while maintaining previous split directions
- Wrote unit tests for DefaultChunkBalancer to check for improvement in load-balancing, convergence to a load-balanced state, and that split_pos values are adjusted correctly for each iteration.
- Wrote unit tests for the MockSimulation class used by the DefaultChunkBalancerTests
- Added a binary_partition_utils.py library which includes lots of tree traversal algorithms which are useful to have for the chunk balancer
- Wrote unit tests for binary_partition_utils.py

author: Matthias Zilk <matthias.zilk@gmail.com>
message:
Changed default integer type to support more than 2^31-1 grid points

Changed the default integer type for grid sizes from int to a 64bit
signed integer type on 64bit systems. This enables using large grids
with more than 2^31 grid points. For maintainability a new typedef
meep::integer is introduced in meep/meeptyes.hpp and is set to
ptrdiff_t. This will ensure the proper sizes on both 32bit and 64bit
systems.

The changes were made according to the following procedure:
- the type of meep::grid_volume::the_ntot was updated to meep::integer
- evrything was recompiled with -Wconversion under gcc4.8.2 on a 64bit
system
- iteratively all places with an implicit conversions from meep::integer
to a smaller interger type where updated until all warnings disappeared
- loop variables were updated from int to meep::integer when a
comparison against meep::integer was involved in the iteration
- all casts to int were checked and corrected where necessary
- additional casts were introduced to silence conversion warnings fron
or to double
- print format specifiers were chenge from %d to %ld with additional
casts to long int to avoid warnings on 32bit systems
- MPI communication wrappers were updated to accept meep::integer as
message size. As MPI specifies only int size messages (and the messages
hopefully will not exceed this limit), internally the size is just
downcasted to int. However, checks of the message size were added before
downcasting to abort when the message size does not allow a safe cast.
This at least ensures a proper error message when the supported message
size is exceeded.

author: Luochenghuang <Luocheng@uw.edu>
message:
Skip MPB for planewave eigenmodes in homogeneous media

When computing diffraction efficiencies via DiffractedPlanewave in get_eigenmode_coefficients, auto-detect if the flux monitor is in a spatially homogeneous medium (by sampling epsilon/mu at the center and edges of the monitor plane). If so, bypass MPB entirely and compute the planewave eigenmode fields analytically.

For homogeneous media the propagating modes are planewaves with analytically known k-vectors (from the dispersion relation k_perp = sqrt(n²ω² - k_parallel²)) and polarization vectors (from the s/p decomposition relative to the plane of incidence). Computing the mode coefficients then reduces to a discrete Fourier transform of the DFT-accumulated monitor fields at these known k-vectors, which is what the overlap integral machinery already does when eigenmode_amplitude returns the analytical exp(ik·r) planewave.

This eliminates the need to create maxwell_data (epsilon grid), call the MPB eigensolver or maxwell_set_planewave, perform FFT-based field computation, and do trilinear interpolation — all of which are unnecessary when the mode fields are known analytically.

The implementation:
- is_homogeneous_on_monitor: samples eps/mu at center + edges
- get_eigenmode_planewave: computes k, vg, E0, H0 analytically
- eigenmode_amplitude: fast path returns E0/H0 * exp(ik·r) directly
- get_eigenmode_coefficients: uses analytical path when dp != NULL and medium is homogeneous; falls back to MPB otherwise

Ref: NanoComp/meep#291

author: Luochenghuang <Luocheng@uw.edu>
message:
Add sinc correction and special_kz fix for analytical planewave

- Apply Yee-grid sinc correction (k_eff = sin(pi*k/a)/(pi/a)) to the analytical E-field computation, making it consistent with the FDTD discretized curl. This is critical for near-grazing modes where k_tangential approaches the Nyquist frequency.
- Fix special_kz detection: also skip analytical path when k[Z] != 0 (kz_2d="complex" mode), not just when beta != 0 ("real/imag" mode).
- Relax test_diffracted_planewave tolerance from places=4 to places=3: the analytical path and band-number MPB use different grids (Yee vs MPB), causing ~1e-4 differences for the most grazing orders.

author: stevenj <stevenj@fftw.org>
message:
rename c -> Courant, make a field of structure instead of global
First of all, I renamed "c" to "Courant", since that is what it is
(Courant number = dt/dx) ... it is not the speed of light, which
should be 1.  (I've run into bugs multiple times now from having "c"
be shadowed by a local variable, e.g. for the component, and this gets
rid of that forever.)

Second, since people may want to change the Courant number to reduce
numerical dispersion (in general, it only has to be < 1 /
sqrt(#dimensions)), I made it a field of the structure class (and also
of structure_chunk and fields_chunk).  The default is still 0.5,
however.

Third, inva is no longer a field of the fields class; instead, we have
a new field dt which is the timestep.  This is much more intuitive and
useful to the end-user (and to us) instead of having to compute
Courant*inva all the time.

There some minor related changes.  e.g. do_harminv takes simply the
sampling interval dt instead of a scale_factor and a.

author: stevenj <stevenj@fftw.org>
message:
make sure coordinates are exact in symmetry.cpp
In symmetry.cpp, we want to check that adding symmetry to a simulation
produces *exactly* the same result as the simulation without explicit
use of symmetry.  This, however, requires a great deal of care with
floating point arithmetic.

In particular, one important requirement is that the sources *exactly*
obey the symmetry condition.  In order for this to be true, the
location of the source *as represented within floating point* must be
symmetric.  (Recall that floating-point can only represent base-2
rational fractions exactly, i.e. integer * 2^e.)  To impose this
condition, we employ two tricks:

First, the resolution 'a' should be exactly representable (e.g. a
power of 2) , so that no surprises occur when converting vecs to ivecs
etc.

Second, the coordinates, or at least those coordinates which are
supposed to be symmetric, must be exactly representable.

For example, suppose that something is supposed to be mirror symmetric
around x=0.5.  You might think that sources at x=0.2 and x=0.8 would
satisfy this, but they don't because those two coordinates are not
exactly representable--they are stored as 0.2+eps1 and 0.8+eps2, where
eps1 and eps2 are ~1e-16, and these coordinates are not symmetric.
Instead, we use e.g. x=0.25 and x=0.75, which are symmetric because
they are exactly represented (1 / 2^2 and 3 / 2^2, respectively).

Of course, a user code is not expected to play these games, but in
such circumstances it is acceptable for the symmetric and
non-symmetric simulations to differ by errors on the order of the
machine precision.

message:
Skip ratio comparison for noise-level values.

The fix: when both power1 and power2 are below 1e-20, skip the ratio comparison entirely — these are noise-level values (like ~1e-38 for the zeroth-order S-pol which is zero by symmetry in the special_kz tests). Dividing noise by noise produces meaningless ratios. When at least one value is significant, we do the ratio check using power2 / power1 directly (safe since power1 > 1e-20).

author: Ben Bartlett <benjamincbartlett@gmail.com>
message:
Implementation of chunk balancer feature (#1775)

* Implementation of chunk balancer feature

CONTEXT: This feature uses empirical data about the timings of each MPI process to adjust the chunk sizes to achieve optimal load balancing for repeated simulations, such as iterations in an optimization run. Processes which are consistently slow and overworked will have their chunk sizes reduced for the next iteration of an optimization run, and underworked processes will handle larger chunks. This approach has the advantage that it implicitly incorporates variable load between different machines running the MPI processes.

SCOPE:
- Added abstract class for chunk balancer
- Added DefaultChunkBalancer implementation, which adjusts chunk sizes according to per-process working time (ignoring all-all comms) while maintaining previous split directions
- Wrote unit tests for DefaultChunkBalancer to check for improvement in load-balancing, convergence to a load-balanced state, and that split_pos values are adjusted correctly for each iteration.
- Wrote unit tests for the MockSimulation class used by the DefaultChunkBalancerTests
- Added a binary_partition_utils.py library which includes lots of tree traversal algorithms which are useful to have for the chunk balancer
- Wrote unit tests for binary_partition_utils.py

author: Luocheng Huang <35114355+Luochenghuang@users.noreply.github.com>
message:
OpenMP parallelize grid initialization (set_epsilon) (#3166)

* OpenMP parallelize grid initialization (set_epsilon)

The grid initialization loop in set_chi1inv iterates over all grid
points to compute the inverse permittivity tensor. At high resolutions
(e.g., 178M points at resolution 200), this takes minutes on a single
core.

Parallelize the loop with OpenMP (PLOOP_OVER_IVECS_C) when the
material function is thread-safe (standard C++ geometry objects, not
Python callbacks). The trivial[] flags use OpenMP reduction.

A new virtual method material_function::is_thread_safe() returns false
by default (safe for Python callbacks). The geom_epsilon subclass
overrides it to return true unless MATERIAL_USER materials are present.

Measured speedup: 30.7s -> 3.2s at resolution 100 (9.7x with 22 cores).
Set OMP_NUM_THREADS to control parallelism.

* Fix lint errors.

author: stevenj <stevenj@fftw.org>
message:
add nonlinear symmetry tests

The nonlinear symmetry tests had been disabled because they caused
the symmmetry.dac test to fail.  I had assumed this was a bug,
but now I'm not so sure.

First, the nonlinear calculations rely on an averaging of field values
from adjacent points, and this averaging process will differ by rounding
errors when using symmetries (e.g. left + right + top + bottom may
change to right + left + top + bottom, which differs by rounding).  So,
I had to decrease the error threshold for the nonlinear tests.

Second, a more serious concern: symmetry is not necessarily preserved
when rounding is included.  A simple example is that exp(i m phi) modes
in a cylindrical waveguide may be converted to exp(3 i m phi) modes
by a Kerr nonlinearity, analogous to 3rd harmonic generation.  I *think*
that this conversion does not occur for the trivial representation
(analogous to m=0), but I'm not 100% sure.  So, the nonlinear tests
(which use the trivial representation, i.e. no phase factor) should
be okay...

However, e.g. the rot4z symmetry test still fails if I use *both* TM
and TE sources (which interact due to the nonlinearity).  Outputting
the fields, it looks like a nonsymmetric pattern really is generated
after a while in this case.   Perhaps this is a numerical effect,
related to the rounding mentioned above?

author: Luocheng Huang <35114355+Luochenghuang@users.noreply.github.com>
message:
Cache `maxwell_data` across `get_eigenmode_coefficients` calls (#3167)

* Cache maxwell_data across get_eigenmode_coefficients calls

When computing diffraction efficiencies, get_eigenmode_coefficients is called separately for each (order, polarization) pair. Each call recreates MPB's maxwell_data and recomputes the epsilon grid, which dominates runtime for structures with many geometry objects.

Add an eigenmode_cache field to dft_flux that persists the maxwell_data across calls to get_eigenmode_coefficients on the same monitor. The first call creates the cache; subsequent calls reuse it. The cache is automatically invalidated when the flux monitor is removed or destroyed.

Also add a skip_phase_fix parameter to get_eigenmode. When called with a DiffractedPlanewave, phase fixing is skipped since |alpha|^2 is phase-invariant (the mode-mode self-overlap normfac cancels any global phase factor).

No Python API changes — the caching is transparent. Partially addresses #1533.

* Skip ratio comparison for noise-level values.

The fix: when both power1 and power2 are below 1e-20, skip the ratio comparison entirely — these are noise-level values (like ~1e-38 for the zeroth-order S-pol which is zero by symmetry in the special_kz tests). Dividing noise by noise produces meaningless ratios. When at least one value is significant, we do the ratio check using power2 / power1 directly (safe since power1 > 1e-20).

* Remove skip_phase_fix for DiffractedPlanewave eigenmodes

The phase-fixing pass in get_eigenmode was being skipped for DiffractedPlanewave mode decomposition under the assumption that |α|² is phase-invariant. However, users may need the phase of α (e.g., for phase delay measurements), so the phase fix must always run to ensure deterministic results.

The eigenmode_cache (maxwell_data reuse) is unaffected — it caches the epsilon grid, while the phase fix operates on freshly computed mode fields each call.

Also fix the cache consistency test to skip comparison when both power values are negligible noise (< 1e-20), since the ratio test is meaningless for symmetry-zero modes like S-pol order 0.

* Handle dispersive materials in eigenmode cache

The eigenmode cache (`maxwell_data` reuse across `get_eigenmode_coefficients` calls) assumed frequency-independent epsilon. For dispersive materials, the cached epsilon grid becomes stale when the eigenmode frequency changes. Detect dispersive media during epsilon grid construction by comparing `get_chi1inv(freq)` vs `get_chi1inv(freq=0)`. When the cache is reused at a different frequency on a dispersive monitor, re-populate the epsilon grid on the existing `maxwell_data` (avoiding full reallocation). New fields on `dft_flux`: `eigenmode_cache_dispersive`, `eigenmode_cache_frequency`. New parameters on `get_eigenmode`/`get_eigenmode_coefficients`: `cache_dispersive`, `cache_frequency` (optional, default NULL for backward compatibility).

* lint

* lint

* Add is_frequency_dependent output parameter to get_chi1inv

Add an optional bool *is_frequency_dependent parameter (default NULL) to all get_chi1inv and get_chi1inv_at_pt overloads across structure_chunk, fields_chunk, fields, and structure. When non-NULL, it is set to true if any susceptibility with non-zero sigma or non-zero conductivity is encountered, allowing callers to detect dispersive materials without extra get_chi1inv calls at frequency=0.

* Use get_chi1inv's is_frequency_dependent flag to detect dispersive materials instead of calling get_chi1inv twice (at freq and at DC) and comparing with a tolerance. Previously missed that get_chi1inv already supports an is_frequency_dependent output parameter.

* Synchronize found_dispersive across MPI ranks with or_to_all

* Remove is_frequency_dependent = false initialization from get_chi1inv_at_pt; caller is responsible for initializing to false so multiple calls naturally accumulate without needing explicit ||.

* Fix no-MPB stub: add missing cache_dispersive and cache_frequency parameters

* Apply suggestion from @stevengj

* Extract populate_maxwell_dielectric helper to deduplicate the two-pass epsilon sampling, MPI synchronization, and MPB upload sequence that was repeated for both initial creation and dispersive-frequency cache updates; also apply clang-format fixes.

* Lint

* Make populate_maxwell_dielectric a fields method so am_now_working_on/finished_working resolve implicitly; use void*/double in header to avoid exposing MPB types.

author: stevenj <stevenj@fftw.org>
message:
completely revamped structure and structure_chunk initialization
In the previous version of the code, the typical initialization
sequence went like this:

1) create structure (initializes chunks, evaluates epsilon)
2) set PML (re-initializes chunks, shuffles epsilon around)

Step (2) is problematic because the communication of epsilon to the
new chunks was performed point-by-point.  Not only is this incredibly
slow, but it actually causes Tungsten's MPI implementation to crash
(probably because there are too many messages).  Moreover, it is
completely unnecessary.

In the new version, the PML boundaries are specified when the structure
is first created, so that the chunks need only be computed once and are
never re-shuffled around.

INCOMPATIBLE API CHANGE:

  old:
     structure s(vol, eps, splitting, symmetries);
     s.use_pml_everywhere(1.0);

  new:
     structure s(vol, eps, pml(1.0), symmetries, splitting);

In general, the PML boundary regions are specified by *summing* terms
of the form pml(thickness, direction, High/Low).  If one or both of
the last two arguments is omitted, it means *all* sides and *all*
directions, respectively.  So, a more complicated example is:

  old:
     structure s(vol, eps, splitting, symmetries);
     s.use_pml(X, High, 1.0);
     s.use_pml(X, Low, 1.0);
     s.use_pml(Y, High, 1.0);

  new:
     structure s(vol, eps, pml(1.0, X) + pml(1.0, Y, High),
                 symmetries, splitting);

To specify *no* PML, you use:

   structure s(vol, eps, no_pml(), symmetries, splitting);

This is actually the default, if you omit the boundary-region argument
along with splitting (default = 0) and symmetries (default =
identity).

INCOMPATIBLE API CHANGE:

  old:
     s.set_epsilon(eps, minvol, do_aniso_averaging);

  new:
     s.set_epsilon(eps, do_aniso_averaging, minvol);

The default for the last two arguments is true and 0, respectively, so
in the usual case where you are using this function because you want
to turn on averaging (currently not the default), you just do:

   s.set_epsilon(eps);

author: stevenj <stevenj@fftw.org>
message:
faster, more easily generalized output_hdf5 based on fields::integrate
The old version of fields::output_hdf5 pre-dated fields::integrate,
and had home-brewed code for looping over the chunks and symmetries
and computing the output from each.  Not only was this complicated (as
opposed to centralizing the complexity in fields::integrate), but it
also was based on fields::interpolate onto an arbitrary grid, which
had the following disadvantages:

* doing an arbitrary interpolation for every point in a large volume
  is very slow.  This is a problem if we want to output often.

* very hard to compute functions of more than one field component,
  e.g. the energy density or the average inveps dielectric, because
  on an arbitrary grid this requires communication in general.

* hard to prevent different chunks/symmetries to write slightly
  overlapping data, which produces undefined results in parallel HDF5.

The new code *always* outputs on the dielectric grid, which (since it
is a fixed interpolation scheme) is a tight loop for each chunk, and
is guaranteed by fields::integrate to be non-overlapping.  Perhaps
even more importantly, it will now be easy to implement output
functions of more than one field component, since no communication is
required for the interpolation.

message:
automate full installation to any directory (not only /usr/local)

This script is very useful for

- users with electromagnetics skills in the need for the latest MEEP developments
  but lacking time to get sufficient system knowledge to reach their grail,

- system administrators constantly being asked for the latest MEEP versions by
  their impatient electromagnetics specialists users (sometimes for years)

This script has his place right in the source repository, so the (large)
audience can improve and adapt it over time.

author: Luocheng Huang <35114355+Luochenghuang@users.noreply.github.com>
message:
OpenMP parallelize susceptibility grid initialization (#3171)

* OpenMP parallelize susceptibility grid initialization (add_susceptibility)

Follow the same parallelization pattern used for set_chi1inv (set_epsilon) in commit d465929d. When the material function is thread-safe (C++ geometry, not a Python callback), use PLOOP_OVER_IVECS_C with collapse(3) and a reduction on the trivial_sigma flags. Fall back to the serial LOOP_OVER_VOL path for non-thread-safe material functions.

* Simplify OMP susceptibility loop body and use bitwise AND reduction for consistency with serial path

* Lint

author: stevenj <stevenj@fftw.org>
message:
major surgery on connect_the_chunks
connect_the_chunks was:
   (a) a major performance bottleneck on multiprocessor systems
   (b) very difficult to modify, consisting of the same code
       copy-and-pasted many times
   (c) fairly fragile, with the loops impossible to reorder
       without breaking step.cc

I've tried to fix all of those problems.  Now, instead of calling
things like locate_point O(nc^2) where np is the number of chunks,
it only computes it O(nc) times, and a lot of the duplication is
removed.  It's also much less fragile, because the connections are
stored per phase type (complex, -1, or +1) rather than in one
order-sensitive array.

However, this required major changes to boundaries.cpp and related code.

message:
Add a POC cumbersome fix for Moodle3_9

This version works when tested manually on all
versions of Moodle and PHP, but more important
on Travis.

It fixes that CI test fail that have been detected on
Moodle3_9 only; while it works perfectly, when tested
manually.

This is a very strange behavior that has been detected
when running behat tests. The MathType client-side
render does not work, ( nor Mathjax ), because the
filter fails to convert right from SafeMathML to
standard MathML.

It generates a wrong MathML format so the WIRISPlugins.js

message:
[KB-3952]: Add new render option with js bundle

The new 'client' options is now available at the plugin settings page.
This setting description has been updated on the lang file.
When selected, the filter does two things:

  1. Filters the text from Full MathML to default MathML
  2. Adds the WIRISplugins.js defined at the 3rd party lib to the page.

The expected behavior is any MathML formula on the page will be
rendered using Javacript.

Context:

- https://wiris.kanbanize.com/ctrl_board/2/cards/3952/details/
- https://wiris.kanbanize.com/ctrl_board/2/cards/3951/details/

- Update  third-party libraries file with the 'Javascript library'.

message:
Add a POC cumbersome fix for Moodle3_9

This version works when tested manually on all
versions of Moodle and PHP, but more important
on Travis.

It fixes that CI test fail that have been detected on
Moodle3_9 only; while it works perfectly, when tested
manually.

This is a very strange behavior that has been detected
when running behat tests. The MathType client-side
render does not work, ( nor Mathjax ), because the
filter fails to convert right from SafeMathML to
standard MathML.

It generates a wrong MathML format so the WIRISPlugins.js
is unable to render it right. It shows an empty image.

This only happens when running on behat scenario, but works
fine if it's tested manually. In moodle3_9 works too. :shrug:

Also:

- Fix MathJax tests to be compatible with these changes.

- Fix lint errors on shome gherkin  tests.

message:
Release 7.26.0

Includes:

- Fix & upgrade TravisCI job configuration
- Update settings description about rendering options
- Use a more consistent way for language strings EOS
  Some language strings add a 'nbsp;' at the end of the
  string.
  This is a bad practice and it's error-prone since it
  passes the responsability to tranlators to avoid
  bad formatting messages on the plugin test
  page: /filter/wiris/info.php.

- Add missing newer PHP versions to TravisCI.
- Enable TravisCI 'fast_finish' option.
- Lint files to pass tests.
- Add optional run docker after install.
- Don't use the blackboard-open-source until it's fixed.
- Simplify exclusion and enviornment on the TravisCI file.
- Update README file.
- Add a test to validate MathType buttons visibility

  Create two tests to check that the math and chem
  buttons are available and can be disabled at any
  time with the atto and tinymce editors.

- Add a function for the visibility settings
- Remove 'filtersettings.php' file: duplicated
- Upgrade version to 7.26.0 (20210416)

  This commit bumps this plugin version to 7.26.
  We've decided to move from 7.24 to 7.26 in oder
  to synchronize version numbers with the rest of
  MathType integrations for HTML editors.

- Add latest Moodle versions to TravisCI pipeline.
- Fix README header logo.
- Fix phpunit validation errors on Moodle3_10+.

author: Rodrigo Tobar <rtobar@icrar.org>
message:
Exposing new pure C++ watershed through Rcpp

We are calling this implementation "water_cpp_new", and exposing it
through the watershed='ProFound-new' option. The implementation is
simple: it creates the segment image, an Rcpp-based interrupt checker,
and passes everything down to our new C++11 watershed implementation.

Once the watershed algorithm is finished we need to add 1 to all
elements, since the C++11 code uses -1 to signal a no-segment cell,
while actual segments are numbered starting from 0. This is different
from the previous implementations, which use 0 to signal a no-segment
cell, and segments were numbered starting from 1.

Signed-off-by: Rodrigo Tobar <rtobar@icrar.org>

author: Rodrigo Tobar <rtobar@icrar.org>
message:
New C++11 header-only watershed implementation

This implementation follows the exact same logic found in the water.cpp
file, but implemented only using standard C++11 constructs and headers.
The implementation is offered as a header-only library to allow easy
reuse, and uses templates to let users provide their own interruption
mechanism for long-running problems.

The implementation requires the user to provide a pre-allocated
segmentation image that should be of the same size as the image to be
watershed. This is important for large images, in which case making
unnecessary copies of the data can exhaust the available resources and
lead to errors.

The code is not only more easily reusable, but also performs better.
This is due to: a) using std::vector instead of Rcpp's Vector classes,
since the former grows more nicely than the latter, b) using
pre-allocated vectors where previously new instances of a Vector would
be re-allocated each time, c) changing the order in which a few
conditions were checked for to allow short-circuiting them, and d)
changing the iteration order for neighboring pixels when watershedding a
particular "central" pixel.

Signed-off-by: Rodrigo Tobar <rtobar@icrar.org>

author: Rodrigo Tobar <rtobar@icrar.org>
message:
Avoid implicit memory allocations in multithreaded contexts

Both pixelCoverPoly and in_poly received their NumericalVector arguments
by value, meaning that a copy of the object was always required (even if
the underlying data they pointed to isn't copied). This object creation
implies a memory allocation, and the R memory allocation isn't
thread-safe, leading to issues in multi-threaded execution contexts.

This commit changes the pixelCoverPoly function to receive its
parameters as const references, hence avoiding the new object creation
in the first place. The in_poly function on the other hand is exported
via Rcpp, therefore a new in_poly_internal function taking the vectors
as const references has been added, which both in_poly and
pixelCoverPoly call internally.

Avoiding these copies also has the very nice effect that performance
increases significantly.

Signed-off-by: Rodrigo Tobar <rtobar@icrar.org>

message:
version 2.1.2 update

Bug fixes:
    * fixed float to integer conversion errors. IndexErrors were raised in zernikemath.py

Command changes:
    *  Added option in Fresnel and Forvard commands to use the pyFFTW or the numpy Fast Fourier Transform package. Default is FFT in numpy. This allows the user to compare the two FFT methods.
    *  Added a config.py file. Here one can make the usage of pyFFTW permanent.
       Change "_USEPYFFTW = False" to "_USEPYFFTW = True" in that file.
       See: :ref:`using_pyFFTW` for more details.

In this version we also install the package matplotlib as a required installation.
Matplotlib is used in almost all LightPipes applications to present the results.

message:
Use Field.copy on F in ZernikeFilter to prevent in-place modification

The line `Fout = F` did not create a copy of F, just a second reference, and the line `Fout.field *= _np.exp(-1j * Ph)` modified the object referenced by both Fout and F, so the input Field also came out filtered.
